core_question: How do we fix the contact form that silently never sends, give the site a language and a real 404, and cut the wallpaper weight, without regressing the deployed build?
knowns: gh secret list returns empty with exit 0, so no NEXT_PUBLIC_EMAILJS_* secret is set; the env vars are undefined at build time, isEmailJsConfigured is false, and every visitor's Send falls back to mailto
The fallback shows the visitor an internal-sounding line, 'Opened your email client because EmailJS is not configured in this environment', which a recruiter reads as a broken form
emailjs-com is a deprecated package superseded by @emailjs/browser, and it is bundled into the 70KB index chunk while never being reachable
out/index.html renders <html> with no lang attribute because the project has no src/pages/_document.tsx
out/404.html is the unstyled Next.js default titled '404: This page could not be found' with no link back to the site
The active wallpapers are animated GIFs at 507KB (2_evening) and 409KB (5_night_totoro), the heaviest first-paint assets on the site
The operator chose three of the four offered items and left the orphaned blog post alone, so Writing stays archived from the UI
Verified sound this pass: desktop icons carry tabIndex, aria-label and Enter/Space handling; every img has alt text; reduced-motion guards, robots.txt, sitemap and JSON-LD are all in place
main is at ecd6285, in sync with origin/main, tree clean, and the last deploy run 35756174292 concluded success
unknowns: If animated WebP conversion drops the wallpaper below acceptable quality, the visual check fails and the GIF has to be kept or re-encoded at a higher quality setting
Should a converted wallpaper fail to animate in the browser, PIL wrote a single-frame WebP and the loop parameters need to be passed explicitly
If npm run build exits non-zero after removing emailjs-com from package.json, an import of that module remains somewhere and the TypeScript error names the file
When the 404 route is added, if GitHub Pages still serves the default page for an unknown path then the export did not emit 404.html at the root and the deploy fails to pick it up
If the rendered html element still lacks lang after adding _document.tsx, the custom document was not picked up and accessibility tooling keeps reporting the error
assumptions: Making mailto the intended contact path is the right call rather than wiring EmailJS, because the operator picked the removal option and a static site with no secret store gains little from a third-party sender
Animated WebP is safe to ship, because every browser that supports the container queries this site already relies on has supported animated WebP for longer
Rollback is cheap by construction: work lands as commits on main off a verified-green ecd6285, and git revert plus a push restores the deployed state within minutes
disconfirmation: If npm run build or npm run lint exits non-zero, or the rendered html element still has no lang attribute, or a converted wallpaper fails to animate in the browser, the change failed and does not get committed as shipped

verification_trace.command: npm run build && npm run lint && grep -c 'lang="en"' out/index.html

patch_vs_refactor_evaluation: Four independent local changes: src/components/ContactForm.tsx drops the emailjs-com import and the env reads in favour of the mailto path it already contains, package.json and .github/workflows/nextjs.yml drop the now-unused dependency and secret block, a new src/pages/_document.tsx supplies the lang attribute, a new src/pages/404.tsx replaces the framework default, and public/images/gif/* plus WALLPAPER_OPTIONS in XPDesktop.tsx swap GIF for WebP. No module boundary moves and no data shape changes, so patch rather than refactor.
